passage: The Petrov group investigated turnover of cyclin B, a regulatory protein that is rapidly degraded in proliferating cells. To measure stability without confounding new synthesis, cells were treated with cycloheximide, an inhibitor of translation elongation, and harvested at the times shown. Lysates were resolved by SDS-PAGE, transferred to a membrane, and probed with an antibody against cyclin B; band intensities were quantified and normalized to a loading control. Degradation of cyclin B was assumed to follow first-order kinetics. The researchers hoped to compare half-lives under normal and stressed conditions and to learn whether proteasome inhibition would stabilize the protein. Results from unstressed cells are shown; each value is the mean of three biological replicates, with errors below 5% of the mean. Equal total protein was loaded in every lane, as confirmed by the loading control. All procedures followed the laboratory's standard operating protocols, and raw data were archived before analysis.

questions.stem: What fraction of cyclin B remains 90 minutes after cycloheximide treatment?
questions.explanation: At 90 min, two half-lives have elapsed (100 → 50 → 25%).
questions.trap: Stopping at one half-life (50%) or counting three (12.5%); 90 min is two half-lives of 45 min, so 100% falls to 50% and then 25%.

questions.stem: Why is cycloheximide used in this experiment?

options.A: It labels the protein for detection by antibody
options.B: It blocks new synthesis so that the loss of existing protein can be followed
options.C: It accelerates proteasomal degradation of all proteins
options.D: It increases transcription of the gene

questions.explanation: Without blocking translation, newly synthesized protein would obscure the decay of the pre-existing pool.
questions.trap: Thinking cycloheximide speeds degradation or labels the protein; it blocks translation so no new cyclin B is made and the decay of the existing pool can be followed.

questions.stem: If the decay continues to be first-order, what percentage of cyclin B remains after 225 minutes?
questions.trap: Miscounting half-lives; 225 min divided by 45 min is 5 half-lives, giving 3.125%, not the value for one more or one fewer half-life.

questions.stem: Which statement about first-order decay is INCORRECT?

options.A: The half-life is independent of starting concentration
options.B: The half-life increases as the starting amount of protein increases
options.C: The rate of decay is proportional to the amount remaining
options.D: The half-life equals ln 2 divided by the rate constant

questions.explanation: In first-order kinetics, t½ = ln 2/k and does not depend on starting concentration.
questions.trap: Choosing a true statement about first-order decay; the half-life is constant (ln 2/k) and does not rise with starting amount, so the claim that it increases is the incorrect one.

questions.stem: cyclin B turnover is typically controlled by which system?

options.B: Phosphorylation by glycolytic kinases that leads to secretion
options.C: Ubiquitination and degradation by the proteasome
options.D: Glycosylation in the Golgi apparatus that prevents degradation

questions.explanation: Polyubiquitin chains (K48-linked) mark proteins for proteasomal degradation; proteasome inhibitors such as MG132 stabilize short-lived regulatory proteins.
questions.trap: Choosing lysosomal, Golgi or secretion mechanisms because they sound like protein fates; short-lived regulatory proteins such as cyclin B are ubiquitinated and degraded by the proteasome.
